ARABIC — TERMLY EXAM #1
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.

2. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.

3. When practising Conversational skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Conversational skills.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational skills.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Conversational skills.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational skills.

4. When practising Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

5. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Only memorise without using the language
   B. Avoid speaking to classmates
   C. Mix random languages with no purpose
   D. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

6. When practising Imitative speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Imitative speaking.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative speaking.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Imitative speaking.

7. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.

8. When practising Speaking Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Speaking Fluency.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Speaking Fluency.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Speaking Fluency.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Speaking Fluency.

9. When practising Selective Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Selective Listening.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Selective Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Selective Listening.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Selective Listening.

10. When practising Reading Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Fluency.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading Fluency.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading Fluency.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
11. In three clear sentences, explain Social Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

12. In three clear sentences, explain : Creative Writing: Compositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

13. In three clear sentences, explain Functional Writing: Formal Letters and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Nawasikh and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Subjunctive and Jussive moods and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Negative Articles أدوات ال نفي and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
